question: Does a 036-only BinDiff-inspired multi-evidence matcher locate manually corrected 043 UI symbols?
prototype_hypothesis: No new prototype is promoted by this experiment; source prototypes remain candidates until target callsite/ABI verification.
callsite_evidence: The matcher uses exact and Thumb relocation-masked entry bytes, CFG shape/topology, strings/constants, size/degree context and caller-neighborhood matching.
The 036 source corpus contributes 126 function-entry records; the 043 target corpus contains 42,246 functions.
The five oracle symbols present in the 036 source pack all match the independently corrected 043 entry addresses.
lvx_content_pad_bottom is source-missing in the 036 symbol pack and is not guessed or counted as a failed address match.
control_flow_evidence: Caller-neighborhood matching compares distinct normalized caller correspondences rather than treating identical 8-byte veneer bytes as unique evidence.
The report retains per-family scores, candidate margins, graph evidence and missing ABI/data-flow evidence.
ownership_analysis: None. This is static candidate-generation evidence only.
unsafe_assumptions: A 5/5 oracle hit does not prove all 123 generated candidates are correct.
The matcher still lacks normalized instruction streams, exact callsite register-flow verification and global/table data-flow proof.
Candidate files are written outside the production symbols directory and must not be used to generate callable bindings.
A static hit is not a device probe or device proof.
recommended_probe: Use the corrected 043 UI addresses in the staged T0-T6 native-app/Launcher device gates only after ABI and descriptor verification.
